drafts.retell: The one where Larry walks you home through the cold and, because an old Tamil book says you do not eat while a guest stands outside, has to bring you up to dinner.
drafts.evidence: MOVES 4. The feeling is something that happens: we are put outside lit glass at `pass-restaurant`, outside it again at `apartment-door`, the question is asked at `q-come-up`, and we are let in by `position`, `buzzed-in`, `chair` and `chair-in`. Nobody says welcome. `cant-fix` ('I can walk you somewhere warm') is a promise the piece then keeps, and `first-snow` after 3.2 s of silence is small and true. Marked down: `assignment` sums up his reading; the viewer is never allowed a harder question than `q-how`; `glance-back` puts a staged gag and a sound between the two halves of the owner's line, which can read as a joke on that line. INTERESTING 4. Retellable and only this special's (the couplet that obliges him). But twelve scenes in four minutes and five crew bits in twenty seconds do not all pass the cut test (list below). TELEVISION 4. The richest street of the three and it meets the words in every scene: shutter and new neon under `shoe-shop`, the gutter under `stream-1`, the drums under `laundry`, the scaffold lamp under `work-1`, the same window twice. All of it is in the staging read as small pieces. Marked down: three source lines on screen that nobody says (at `gutter-stream`, `pass-scaffold`, and the label under `guest-1`); things that move by themselves in shot (`chair-in`, `lid-off`); `gutter-stream` frames 'beside his feet' when only a chest-up walk exists; `buzzed-in` uses a sound the writer says may be heard as a wrong answer. LARRY 4. Dry, kind, a reader and not an expert (`wasnt-here`, `stretched`, 'As I remember it' at `guest-1`), and the best staging of the question device: he turns, holds, says it back (`listen-how`), and once answers a look without repeating it (`the-look`). Marked down: he puts a tag on nearly every scene (`wasnt-here`, `weekend`, `story`, `laundry`, `better-one`, `this-morning`, `sibyl-would`, `position`), about one every fifteen seconds, which is the host at work where the outline asks for a man slower to joke. The crew are themselves to a fault: `chair`, `pete-says`, `record`, `dee-sings` in a row is a roll call, as the writer's own worry says. IDEAS 4. Tarfon is usable tonight and given room (`work-1` to `assignment`, with 2.6 s of silence and `used-book` after it). The Tirukkural telling is the best use of an idea in the three drafts because it is an act, not a lesson (`guest-1`, `guest-2`, `position`). The Hojoki is displayed and its answer declined (`hut`, `weekend`); 'unceasingly' and three hard names (Kamo no Chomei, Tarfon, Tirukkural) lean on the caption. Japanese, Jewish, Tamil, and three different relations to a book (argues, borrows, obeys), so not a list. Attributions read as the cards' safe wordings and both quotations match their cards. For the auditor: `position` is a light line straight after a text whose card says not to joke about the book; the joke is on Larry, but it should be looked at.
wouldNotBeMissed: `poet` to `weekend` (the Hojoki block, with `gutter-stream`): the one idea Larry does not use; `old-books` has already said that people were rattled before us
`eppy-counts` and `dee-sings`: the fourth and fifth welcome in twenty seconds, after `chair-in` has already seated us
`better-one`: a join that explains the laundry line was not the idea
the three source lines on screen (`gutter-stream`, `pass-scaffold`, the label at `guest-1`): unspoken text over a personal walk
`coin`: a pause and a sound between two halves of the busker scene; `out-here` has made the point
drafts.fixedPoints: ok. All five owner's lines are in their places, the viewer never speaks, the holiday and its food are not named, and the last words are the owner's. My count is 414 spoken words plus 18 sung, 432 by the brief's count; about 235 to 250 s. One note: the owner's table line is split across `larry-to-us` and `glance-back` with a cue, a sound and a staged look between its halves; the other two drafts run it unbroken.
drafts.reason: Nothing in its lines, devices, images, opening or close does a job an aired episode did. Looked at and passed, for the script gate to look at again: (1) `shoe-shop`/`wasnt-here` step back through two 'before that's; 002-2026-w47's making-of ran a six-rung 'Before X: Y.' ladder, which the ledger lists as a spent form. Two steps of ordinary speech with a different turn (he is the newcomer), not the ladder, but it is the nearest thing in the draft. (2) `glance-back` has Pete tapping on glasses just before the goodnight; the previous aired episode closed on a toast gesture and a goodnight. As written it is drumming that Sibyl stops, not a toast; it must not be staged as one. (3) `dee-sings` is a new four-note aside, not a returning hook with a changed word, so it is not the song device that has aired twice; her look 'from Larry to us' is the same direction of address as that hook's last pass and is a staging choice to watch. (4) `busker-song` ('One more song, then...') is a lyric with its own joke, not the stock join the previous episode used before its song. (5) `cant-fix` is an offer, not the joke that he is only a host. (6) Eppy's count and record, Sibyl's ruling and Hy speaking for Pete are the cast chapter's natures with new content. (7) Common to all three drafts and not the writers' doing: the scarf 'draws itself' on, and the pilot's host had his tuxedo draw itself on as a gag. Here it is the owner's stage direction done without hands, a different job; the staging read's other option (cut to the collar as it settles) avoids the echo. The gold scarf is his colour and carries no punch. The closing 'folks' and 'Goodnight' are the owner's lines and frame by the owner's ruling.

drafts.retell: The one where Larry is asked what if none of it ever gets put right, says he does not know, borrows an old rabbi's line about not finishing and not quitting, and the light turns to WALK.
drafts.evidence: MOVES 4. The truest exchange in the three drafts: `q-put-right` is the question the special exists for, `dont-know` refuses to fake an answer, the borrowed line comes only then (`tarfon-1`, `tarfon-2`, `dont-finish`, `dont-quit`), and `didnt-arrange` puts the lightness within a beat, where it belongs and in his voice. `no-joke` and `i-looked` are the off-air man in two lines. The viewer's silent yes before `scarf` is a good small thing. Marked down: `cook-keep` sums up what was just shown; `walk-sign` is a swell made out of a traffic light; `house-rule` states the welcome as a principle; arriving is one line (`this-is-me`). INTERESTING 4. Two things a viewer would tell someone: the cook who slows down on the word, and the light that changes after the rabbi's line with 'I didn't arrange that.' The cut test finds the Marcus block and the steam grate. TELEVISION 5. Three pictures land on their words (`window-dark`, `cook-slows`, `walk-sign`), the camera takes the chair at `sit`, there are 5 s of snow with no words at `cross`, and the only text on screen is OPEN, DON'T WALK and WALK. Everything asked for is in the staging read. Risks, not faults: the cook is a small silhouette at the back of a window on a phone; `crossing-red` to `walk-sign` is about forty seconds in one place and lives on its shot changes; from `windows` to `window-dark` it is a voice over sliding fronts. It also asks least of the singing voice: the tune has no words. LARRY 4. Dry, never the expert (`zhuangzi-name`, 'The way I remember it' at `cook-prince`, `tarfon-borrow`), kind (`good-one`), and at `asked-put-right` the question device is used for what the outline wants it for: he says the question back because it is heavy. Marked down: honest but hardly personal, which the outline asks for by name; `q-all-right` is question and answer in one breath; the crew are themselves (`late` without looking up, `house-record`, `sit-eat`) but there is little of them, and Pete never speaks. IDEAS 5. Each is an answer for tonight or tomorrow morning, said plainly after its source (`marcus-quote`; `cook-hard-part`, `cook-gently`; `dont-finish`, `dont-quit`), each is tied to a thing seen, and `what-helped` frames them as help and not as learning. Roman, Chinese, Jewish; they arrive from the street and from a question, not from a list. Attributions read as the cards' safe wordings and both quotations match their cards. `cook-keep` ('things speed up') is Larry's own gloss and not the story's; he says 'I keep that one', which owns it. The translations quoted are named nowhere a viewer can see.
wouldNotBeMissed: `windows` to `tomorrow-then` (the Marcus block): the least tied to the street; the picture is someone going to bed under words about getting up
`walk-on`: the steam grate is decoration between two scenes
`full-house`: a line that only points at the picture
`house-record` and `dee-laughs`: a second beat on his lateness
drafts.fixedPoints: ok. All five owner's lines are in their places and the last three run unbroken at the table; the viewer never speaks (footsteps only); the holiday and its food are not named. My count is 400 spoken words plus 15 sung in `sing` beats, 415 by the brief's count, with Dee's seven in the music block on top: at the floor of the range. About 245 s.
drafts.avoid: `larry-hums`, `hy-flat` and the way `table-tune` answers them: Larry singing or humming a note that comes out wrong, the bandleader remarking on it, and the band's music then putting it right, as the last thing before the goodnight. Also `waited-for-crowd`: a tag in which Larry measures himself against someone who has just made something and comes off the lesser. The busker's tune itself, and Dee ending it, are clear.
drafts.reason: Two items; the rest is fresh. (1) Device and close. 002-2026-w47, the previous aired episode, ended with the band turning to Larry, his one unsure note that was not the one wanted, Hy's dry line taking it, the band's music making it come home, a few lines and the goodnight. The ledger records that shape as aired in both episodes, judged a repeat once already and kept by the owner, and lists it under signatures in the making. Here, in the same position: Larry's hum lands a semitone under (`larry-hums`), Hy answers it drily (`hy-flat`), the band takes it up and lands the home note (`table-tune`), a few lines, the goodnight. One sentence covers both without naming a subject. It is not a turn: the band correcting him instead of fitting itself to him varies the earlier ending and does not defeat it, and the feeling (the band a step ahead, taking him in) is the same. `late` hangs on it through 'also'. (2) Joke. `waited-for-crowd` is the same premise and turn as a line in that episode's interview, where a guest had simply made the thing and Larry said what he does instead; it even opens on the same two words. Looked at and passed: `mostly-lights` is one joke about the show, inside the limit of one; `no-joke`/`i-looked` is new; the chirp at `walk-sign` is the crossing's own sound and the undercut is a line, not the pilot's animal call after a sincere beat; Eppy's record and Sibyl's house rule are natures with new content; the scarf and the gold as for writer-1.

drafts.retell: The one where a busker has been one line short of a song since the spring, and when Larry gets home his friends have held dinner and Dee sings the missing line.
drafts.evidence: MOVES 4. The highest single moment in the three drafts is `comrade-line` to `poem-talking`: he tells us he is glad of the company in someone else's words, cannot look at us while he does (`comrade`, `glance`), and half takes it back. `how-have-you-been` with `yeah-me-too`, and `comes-out`, are plain and true. Marked down: three places tell (`same-worries`, `that-for-one`, `no-last-line` with `what-youve-got`); the payoff at `saved-a-seat` lands only if sung words are heard or read; the last picture is from the step in the snow, with a seat saved and nobody in it. INTERESTING 4. The strongest one-sentence story of the three. The cut test finds the Analects block and the bus. TELEVISION 3. Good pictures on the word (`doorman-nods`, `dessert`, `crossing-walk` on 'cue', the tilt at `glance`). But the spine is carried by five sung beats with words (`busker-1` to `busker-4`, `saved-a-seat`), the thing the engine does worst, so the story has to be read off the lyric line on a phone; `quote` is a still head for about fifteen seconds; `last-block` is sliding windows under talk. All of it can be staged. LARRY 5. The most personal and the most himself: `mail-it`, `meant-kindly`, `guest`, `a-cue`, `poem-talking`. The best table: `house-rule`, `my-house`, `still-the-rule`, `long-way` and `counted-in` are people who have known each other for years, and nobody says so. The question device is conversation at `how-have-you-been`; `what-do-i-do` and `does-it-help` answer in the same breath and sound like a figure of speech. IDEAS 4. Tarfon is tied to the unfinished song and carried in the first person (`finish-quit`); the Havamal line is an offering and not a lesson; the Analects idea is not clear on one hearing (`gatekeeper`: 'the times won't let it work' has no 'it') and is the displayed one. Chinese, Jewish, Norse; not a list. Attributions read as the cards' safe wordings and both quotations match their cards. `guest` says 'study, in his own tradition' where the card says the study and practice of Torah: vaguer, not wrong.
wouldNotBeMissed: `lobby-ahead` to `meant-kindly` (the Analects block): the idea does not come clear on one hearing, and the doorman's nod is the reason it is there
`that-for-one`: points at the moral the busker is already showing
`both-ways`: a look that repeats the empty road
drafts.fixedPoints: ok on the lines, the silent viewer, the unnamed holiday and the last words. My count is 412 spoken words plus 22 sung, 434; about 240 s. One note: the brief put the mixed-up-world line 'at the table'; here all three closing lines are said from the doorway (`goodnight`), with the table behind him and Larry never seated.
drafts.avoid: `no-fix`: Larry excusing himself by naming his job, that he only hosts. `busker-3`: 'doo' as the syllable that stands in for missing words. `saved-a-seat`: a closing sung line that brings back an earlier sung line with new words that turn to 'you' and take the listener in.
drafts.reason: Three items, the first one certain. (1) Joke. `no-fix` ('I host a talk show') is the previous aired episode's 'I only host.' with a longer tail: something more is wanted of him and the answer is his job. The ledger's note for this gate says in terms that a joke whose punch is that he is only a host has been made. (2) Catchphrase on screen. That episode's song made 'doo' its hook, put it on cards and gave it to Larry as his one note seven times over; `busker-3` shows 'doo doo doo' as a lyric six days later, again as filler for having no more. (3) Device, and the reason I am not sure the draft's best idea passes. Both aired songs ended on a sung line coming back with a word changed, a change of person that took the listener in; the ledger lists it as aired twice. `saved-a-seat` brings the busker's line back from where it stopped, with words that turn to 'you', sung to the viewer's chair. And the busker's arc (`what-hes-got`, `what-youve-got`: offering the little you have, and someone else working with it) is the previous song's theme by another road. Fail what is not sure. Looked at and passed: `a-cue`, Eppy's record, Pete's line, Sibyl's house rule against Larry in his own home, the gold chair (his colour as a marker, no punch), the scarf as for writer-1.

why: writer-2, by a little, and with work to do. It is the draft that does what the outline asks in the outline's tone: Larry says he looked for a joke and did not find one, the viewer gets to ask the question the special exists for and he admits he does not know before he borrows an answer, and each of the three ideas is something a person could do, seen happening in the street on its word. It puts least on screen to read and asks least of the singing voice. It goes forward with a repeat to take out at the stair and the table, and with the thinnest table and the least personal Larry of the three. writer-1 is the only draft that is fresh at the gate and has the better door and table; writer-3 has the more personal Larry and the best crew; what each does that the pick does not is under fromOthers. Good enough to go forward once the reasons below are answered; not ready as it stands.
sendBack: Repetition gate, see `avoid` for writer-2: `larry-hums`, `hy-flat` and the way `table-tune` answers them, and `waited-for-crowd`. `late` leans on `hy-flat` through the word 'also'. With those out, nothing at the table tells a viewer that the tune Dee sings is the street's.

`windows` to `tomorrow-then` (the Marcus block): the weakest meeting of street and words. The words are about getting up and the picture is someone going to bed; `tomorrow-then` gives the viewer under two seconds to work out whose 'Fine' it is; until `window-dark` it is a voice over sliding fronts for about fifteen seconds. On the cut test it is the idea a viewer would miss least.
`cook-keep`: says in words what `cook-slows` has just shown, and 'I keep that one' is a summing-up. The picture had already landed.

`walk-sign`: the sign changes on the last word of the borrowed line, with a chirp, a head tip and a 1.4 s hold. `didnt-arrange` disowns it and is the right lightness in the right place, but as cued the street is still applauding him. It is the nearest thing in the draft to a swell.

The table, `table-wide` to `sit`: the outline asks for a large group of close friends sharing a meal. What is there is a lateness gag (`late`, `house-record`), a ruling and two words. Nothing is served, passed or eaten, Pete never speaks, Hy and Dee have nothing to do once the tune is over, and the room of friends is 2.6 s of murmur at `sit`. It reads as a welcome party, not a dinner that was already going.

`house-rule`: 'There is always one extra chair' states the welcome as a principle. Sibyl's voice nearly saves it, but it is the one line in the draft that says what the evening means, and it is the title too.

`home-street` and `this-is-me`: coming in costs one line. Nothing on the walk has made it a question whether the viewer comes up, so arriving is a change of place and not something that happens to us.

Larry is honest here but not personal, and the outline asks for personal by name: apart from `headed-home` and the line that goes at the gate, he tells us nothing of himself, where he met these books, or what the walk is to him.

`q-all-right`: question and answer are one beat with no hold before it, so the first use of the device sounds like a figure of speech and not like a question heard. `asked-put-right` is staged as listening; this one is not.

The tune (`busker-far`, `busker-near`, the reprise asked for in the comment at `walk-past`, `table-tune`): its payoff asks a viewer to know a wordless seven-note melody again some seventy seconds later, in the engine's singing voice, with no picture to carry it. It is the writer's own worry and nothing in the script answers it. The sung beats also put a row of 'la' on the lyric line for about ten seconds.

For the project manager and the auditor, not the writer: the two quotations (`marcus-quote`, `tarfon-1` with `tarfon-2`) name no translation anywhere a viewer can see; the busker needs a voice that is not Al's; the stock title and end cards would put a lit studio before the dark one and after the table.

fromOthers.what: Makes coming in an event. The viewer is put outside lit glass at the restaurant (cue `pass-restaurant`) and outside it again at his own building (cue `apartment-door`), the question of coming up is asked, and an old text is the reason he cannot leave us on the pavement: the one place in the three drafts where an idea is something Larry does instead of something he tells. Then the door opens from upstairs (cue `buzzed-in`): somebody saw him coming.

The welcome is done, not stated: a held look (cue `heads-to-us`), one word, a place arriving in front of the camera (cue `chair-in`), the guest served first, and the dish opened with every head leaning in (cue `lid-off`). A meal starts while we are there.

The question device staged as listening: he turns and holds a second as if we had spoken before he says it back (cue `listen-how`), and once he answers a look without repeating anything (cue `the-look`), which keeps the device from wearing.
After the quotation has had its silence, two short lines say where he met it and that he has stretched it: personal, and never the expert.

Larry tells the viewer he is glad of the company in a line that is not his, looks straight ahead while he says it, glances and half takes it back (cues `comrade`, `glance`). The most personal moment in the three drafts, and the feeling is carried by where his head points, not by a statement.
He asks, the viewer answers in a silence we do not hear, and he agrees. The shared unease is set down without either of them naming it.

Two lines that are his alone: why he came in for an envelope they would have posted, and an acknowledgement that the borrowed sentence belongs to a living tradition, in words worth hearing for themselves.

The crew talk to him and across him as people who have known him for years: forty-one minutes waited and called like a result, a drummer's complaint, a ruling he loses in his own home, Hy knowing where he has been. Friends, and nobody says so. Nothing has been touched on the table, which is how we learn they waited.

measure: Show the finished special once, with sound, to three people who have not read it: it worked if at least two can say back in their own words one thing Larry offered that a person could do tonight and what happened when he got home, and if none of them, asked to point at a moment where they were told how to feel, can point at a line of Larry's other than the owner's closing lines.
